image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of an African crocodile (Nile crocodile) resting on a light-colored stone or concrete ledge. The head is prominent on the left, showing a closed mouth with visible teeth, textured skin, and a dorsal eye. The body extends to the right, displaying heavy, armored scutes. A single forelimb with dark claws is visible tucked against the body. The background is a blurred, out-of-focus sandy or earthy area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed, but several large, conical teeth from the lower jaw are clearly visible protruding upwards along the jawline, matching the description of interlocking teeth visibility.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye is positioned dorsally, the resolution and angle do not allow for clear verification of vertical slit pupils or the presence of a nictitating membrane. The eye appears somewhat glossy/obscured.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are clearly visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with the anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows thick, raised scales indicative of heavy armor. The elongation is implied by the framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface exhibits distinct, raised, bony-looking scutes. While the full longitudinal row pattern is partially obscured by the angle, the texture and arrangement are consistent with osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of grey and dark tones, and the texture is visibly rough and pebbled.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral surface (belly) is not visible in this side-profile shot; the crocodile is resting on its belly/side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only one forelimb is partially visible. It is impossible to count the digits accurately or see the webbing structure clearly due to the angle and the limb being tucked/resting. Hind limbs are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame of the image.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The eye lacks the sharp, reflective clarity typical of a real reptile eye. It appears slightly 'muddy' or painted-on, lacking a distinct pupil definition, which is a common subtle AI artifact in close-ups.

The visible forelimb appears to merge into the body scales without a clear joint or anatomical separation. The digits look like fused blobs rather than distinct toes, suggesting a minor structural generation error.
The very tip of the snout seems to curve slightly unnaturally downwards, possibly a minor warping issue, though it could be perspective.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species classification based on fine-grained features like snout shape and scute pattern.
To verify the connectivity of the forelimb to the body and ensure no floating scales or boundary bleeding.
To assess the realism of the skin texture and eye reflection, checking for subtle generative smoothness or noise patterns.
To ensure the crocodile sits correctly on the ledge with proper contact shadows and depth separation from the background.

focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of the visible forelimb (digit count and separation)
Realism of the eye texture and pupil definition
Consistency of scute patterns and transitions between body parts
Contact shadows between the crocodile and the stone ledge
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the forelimb. AI often struggles with reptile digits, merging them into a paddle-like shape. Verify if the 'fused' appearance is an artifact or just occlusion. Also, scrutinize the eye; real crocodile eyes have a very specific reflective quality and pupil shape that AI often blurs or simplifies.
